name: flight-track
title: Flight Track
description: A flight card whose route fills with a glowing line behind a small plane with blinking wing lights.

perf.budget: The plane rocks and its lights blink on the UI thread; the route only animates when progress changes. One small Skia canvas for the plane.

measurements.notes: Animating at rest: the plane rocks and its wing lights blink while it is in the air; both stop once landed.

a11y.reducedMotion: The plane jumps to its place, does not rock and its lights stay on.
a11y.screenReader: One progress bar reading the route and times ("LHR, London, UK, to OPO, Porto, PT. Departs 20:50 GMT+1, arrives 22:40 GMT+1.") with "55% of the way".

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { FlightTrack } from '@/components/kinetik/flight-track';

<FlightTrack
  from={{ code: 'LHR', city: 'London, UK', time: '20:50', zone: 'GMT+1' }}
  to={{ code: 'OPO', city: 'Porto, PT', time: '22:40', zone: 'GMT+1' }}
  progress={elapsed / duration}
/>;
```

## When to use

- Live flight or trip status in a travel app, a booking or a widget.
- Any journey between two points with a known start and end time: deliveries, train legs, transfers.

## When not to use

- Journeys with stops: one route line cannot show them. Show a timeline instead.
- When progress is unknown: an estimate that jumps backwards confuses people.

## Notes

- `progress` is yours to compute (for example elapsed time over scheduled time). Each change glides the plane along the route.
- Below 460 pt wide the times move under the route so the codes keep their size.
- The plane is the Tabler Icons plane (MIT licence, via iconstack.io).

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add flight-track`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
